title: Debugging Techniques for CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Start with the simplest possible test to isolate issues quickly.
Use print statements selectively to avoid output spam.
Employ runtime assertions to check invariants within kernels.
Validate inputs and outputs before and after kernel execution.
Compare kernel outputs with a reference implementation to identify discrepancies.
Incrementally build and test kernel components to isolate bugs.
code_snippets:
def validate_and_launch(kernel, data, expected_min=None, expected_max=None):
    print("Pre-launch validation:")
    print(f"  Shape: {data.shape}")
    kernel.launch(grid=[10,1,1], block=[256,1,1])(cute.from_dlpack(data))

@cute.kernel
def complex_kernel(data: cute.Tensor):
    tid = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
    value = data[tid]
    cute.printf("After load: %f\n", value)
    value = process_a(value)
    cute.printf("After process_a: %f\n", value)
constraints: Avoid debugging with large datasets; use small test cases.
Ensure print statements are controlled to prevent excessive output.
Always validate kernel inputs and outputs for NaN or Inf values.
Use systematic debugging approaches to isolate bugs efficiently.
Incremental development helps in identifying which change introduces a bug.
compressed_summary: Debugging GPU kernels using CuTe DSL involves several strategic approaches to efficiently identify and resolve issues. Key techniques include print debugging, runtime assertions, isolating problems, reducing test cases, and comparing outputs with reference implementations. Start with the simplest possible test case to quickly isolate issues, and use print statements selectively to avoid output spam. Assertions can be used within kernels to check for invariant conditions, helping to catch errors early. Validate inputs and outputs before and after kernel execution to ensure data integrity. Comparing kernel outputs with a known-good reference implementation is crucial for identifying discrepancies. Incremental development is recommended, where each component is built and tested separately to isolate bugs effectively. Tools like cuda-memcheck, compute-sanitizer, and cuda-gdb are valuable for detecting memory errors, race conditions, and performance bottlenecks. The systematic approach involves observing the problem, hypothesizing potential causes, testing with added checks, analyzing results, making targeted fixes, and verifying the solution. This structured method, combined with practical debugging tools, forms the backbone of effective debugging in CuTe DSL.
